title: Integral section injectivity at a closed geometric point of a strictly henselian base
statement: Let A be a strictly henselian local ring, Lambda a commutative ring, p:Z -> Spec A an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and F an etale sheaf of Lambda-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For an algebraically closed field Omega and t:Spec Omega -> Spec A with image the closed point, let (i:Z' -> Z,p':Z' -> Spec Omega,p,t) be Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Then the canonical inverse-image unit map on global sections Gamma(Z,F) -> Gamma(Z',i^*F) is injective. No finite-type, torsion, or nonempty-fibre assumption is made.

source.place: Tags 09XK, 09ZH and 0A3I; henselian degree-zero consequence used for the integral comparison

proof.text: Read Spec.preimage t as a ring map and use ht to show m_A is in its kernel. Construct the quotient lift ψ : κ(A) → Ω and r=Spec ψ. Prove r ≫ s=t, where s=Spec(A→κ(A)). Form Z₀=Z×_Aκ(A) and construct j:Z′→Z₀ by pullback.lift. Pullback pasting proves (j,p′,p₀,r) Cartesian.
Apply integralHenselianClosedFibreSections_injective to i₀:Z₀→Z, then etaleModuleSectionsFieldExtension_injective to j and i₀*F, using separable closedness of the residue field of A.

Use globalSectionsUpperStarMap_comp′ for i=j≫i₀. Evaluate the equality at two sections. Equality after i implies equality after the two successive restrictions; their injectivity gives equality of the original sections.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09XK, 0A0C and 0A3I; explicit quotient factorization, pullback pasting and composition of the two restrictions in Lean.
